prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1172; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received on the rear-end collision involving the insured vehicle. The claimant reports a concussion and is now represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and spoke with two independent witnesses, who both describe the other vehicle stopping abruptly and being struck from behind. Photos from the scene line up with that account.

Entry 3: Inspected the damaged vehicle. The rear bumper, trunk lid and tail lamp assembly show crush and impact patterns consistent with the reported speed and direction of the collision.

Entry 4: Confirmed with the police and both witnesses that the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact. The driver is named on the policy and coverage was in force on the loss date.

Entry 5: Ran a prior-claims search and found no earlier damage recorded on this vehicle. Records show no earlier injury claims involving the same body area for the claimant.

Entry 6: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided the medical summary. The concussion diagnosis and the symptoms described fit the force of a collision of this type.

Entry 7: Reviewed treatment records. Care followed a typical course of rest, follow-up visits and gradual reduction in frequency as symptoms improved, with discharge noted after recovery.

Entry 8: Took a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account of the collision matches what was told to the police, the other driver and the witnesses, and has stayed the same in every conversation.

Entry 9: Reviewed all information gathered to date. Damage, injury and the accident account are consistent with one another, and nothing points to a pre-existing condition or prior damage. File remains open pending final medical bills.
